relevance_note: This pediatric liver-disease WES cohort reports one child with a TNFAIP3 variant: 'One patient with Familial Behçet-Like Autoinflammatory Syndrome caused by a TNFAIP3 mutation received infliximab treatment'.
method_note: Read the full Markdown manually; no table transcription by script (a short script only assembled the JSON). Scope: only the single TNFAIP3 carrier was extracted; the other 79 cohort children (variants in ATP7B, JAG1, ABCD3, etc.) are out of HA20 scope and were not given rows. The paper gives no label for this child, so 'patient' is used. The TNFAIP3 variant itself (cDNA/protein, zygosity, inheritance, ACMG class) is not in the text; the paper refers to 'Supplementary Table 1' and to Figure 2 (which encodes zygosity graphically), neither of which is in the Markdown, so those fields are 'not reported'. Pathogenicity: the authors attribute the syndrome to the mutation ('caused by a TNFAIP3 mutation') but do not say whether it is one of the 53 P/LP variants or one of the 7 VUS (46 patients with genetic results vs 42 with P/LP), so pathogenicity_as_stated_by_authors is 'not reported'. Cohort-wide statements applied to this child: consanguinity 'no' ('No consanguineous marriages were found in the cohort.'), vital status 'alive' ('All patients survived during the follow-up'), ethnicity (Chinese pediatric population), and parental testing (methods: 'WES was performed in the patients and their parents'; no per-patient result given, and the VUS paragraph implies parental samples were not available for everyone). Phenotypes from explicit group membership/definitions, all marked 'inferred from group statement': the child is in Group A (liver enzyme elevation group), so elevated liver enzymes observed; Group A by definition excludes children with both elevated enzymes and cholestasis (assigned to Group B), so cholestasis excluded; study exclusion criteria removed autoimmune hepatitis and autoimmune sclerosing cholangitis, so both excluded (AIH also on the checklist). Other exclusion criteria (biliary atresia, drug-induced hepatotoxicity, NAFLD, infectious causes of transaminase elevation such as viral hepatitis, EBV, CMV) also apply by design but were not emitted as feature rows; infectious-cause exclusion does not exclude the broader 'recurrent infections' item. Infliximab treatment and transaminase normalization are stated jointly for the TNFAIP3 and FLG patients ('Both patients showed normalization...'). Minor internal inconsistency (not about this child): the abstract/results report genetic results in 46 patients while the Figure 2 legend says 45 children. No contradictions found about the TNFAIP3 patient.
